definition_en: extreme greed for wealth or material gain
core_image: 攥紧钱袋的手，指缝里漏不出一枚铜板
scene: 老人数完铜板又锁上箱底。His avarice kept him from giving even a coin.
sceneCN: 这里 avarice 指「贪财、吝啬」（第 1 个义项：对财富的极度贪婪）；句意：他的贪婪让他连一枚硬币也舍不得给。

senses.title: Extreme greed for money
senses.definition: an intense, often contemptible desire to accumulate money and keep it
senses.definitionCN: 对积聚并保有金钱的强烈、常遭鄙夷的欲望
senses.example: Avarice kept the miser counting coins into old age.
senses.exampleCN: 贪财让守财奴数着铜板直到暮年。
senses.why: The Latin root avidus means eager; eagerness fixed on money became the vice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 avidus 意为「渴望」，这份渴望一旦锁死在钱上便成了恶习。

senses.title: Greed for any material gain
senses.definition: greedy appetite for property, land, or advantage beyond money itself
senses.definitionCN: 对钱财之外的土地、财产或利益的贪求
senses.example: The empire's avarice reached for its neighbor's mines.
senses.exampleCN: 帝国的贪欲伸向邻邦的矿脉。
senses.why: What greed grabs need not be coins; any holding stretches the word.
senses.whyCN: 贪婪攫取的不一定是钱币，任何财物都能延伸这个词。

senses.title: A vice in moral writing
senses.definition: one of the classical deadly sins, cupidity as a named vice
senses.definitionCN: 古典「七宗罪」体系中的贪欲之罪
senses.example: Medieval preachers set avarice against charity.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪布道者以贪婪与仁爱相对。
senses.why: Moral systems needed a name for hoarding as sin, and Latin supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 道德体系需要为「囤积成罪」命名，拉丁语提供了这个词。

senses.title: Hoarding without use
senses.definition: keeping wealth locked away instead of spending or sharing it
senses.definitionCN: 把财富锁起来而不消费、不分享
senses.example: His avarice let the granaries rot while tenants starved.
senses.exampleCN: 他贪吝囤粮，任谷仓腐坏而佃户挨饿。
senses.why: Greed is not appetite but refusal to let go; the image is the sealed chest.
senses.whyCN: 贪婪不在攫取而在不肯放手，画面是那口上锁的箱子。

senses.title: Motivating corruption
senses.definition: greed cited as the motive behind betrayal or dishonest dealing
senses.definitionCN: 作为背叛或不端交易动机的贪利之心
senses.example: The court heard that avarice, not ideology, sold the secrets.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭查明，出卖机密是出于贪利而非意识形态。
senses.why: When money explains an act, the abstract noun names the reason.
senses.whyCN: 当金钱足以解释一个行为时，抽象名词便来命名这个动机。

senses.title: In satire and caricature
senses.definition: the personified greedy figure, as in satires and allegories
senses.definitionCN: 讽刺与寓言中被拟人化的贪婪角色
senses.example: The play mocked avarice in a moneybag-shaped old man.
senses.exampleCN: 该剧用钱袋形的老者讥讽贪婪。
senses.why: Vices become characters once named; avarice wore the purse.
senses.whyCN: 恶习一旦被命名便化为人形，贪婪佩上了钱袋。

senses.title: Collective or institutional greed
senses.definition: the greed of institutions, corporations, or nations as a collective vice
senses.definitionCN: 机构、公司或国家层面的集体贪欲
senses.example: Public anger blamed corporate avarice for the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 公众把危机归咎于企业的贪得无厌。
senses.why: An abstract vice attaches easily to an abstract actor like the firm.
senses.whyCN: 抽象恶习极易挂在公司这类抽象行为者身上。

senses.title: Self-destructive greed
senses.definition: greed that destroys its own holder, ruin by hoarding or grasping
senses.definitionCN: 终将反噬其主的贪欲，因攫取与囤积而自毁
senses.example: Avarice devoured the family that once owned everything.
senses.exampleCN: 贪欲吞噬了那个曾坐拥一切的家庭。
senses.why: Tradition teaches that the grip tightens until it strangles the hand.
senses.whyCN: 传统训诫说，攥得越紧，越会勒住自己的手。

intro.en: Avarice comes from Old French avarice, from Latin avaritia, built on avarus, greedy, from avere, to crave or desire eagerly.
intro.cn: avarice 经古法语 avarice 出自拉丁语 avaritia，其基础是 avarus「贪婪的」，词根为 avere「热切渴望」。

items.en: The root behind avere has been reconstructed as a stem of wishing or being eager.
items.cn: avere 背后的词根被重构为「希求、热切」之干。

items.en: avere meant to desire eagerly; avarus described one who craves and hoards.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avere 意为热切渴望；avarus 形容渴求并囤积之人。

items.en: avaritia named greed as a vice, one of the capital sins in Christian moral lists.
items.cn: avaritia 指作为恶习的贪婪，在基督教道德清单中列为重罪之一。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as avarice with the same moral weight.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 avarice，道德分量不变。

items.en: Middle English borrowed avarice in the thirteenth century for the vice of greed.
items.cn: 中古英语于 13 世纪借入 avarice，指贪婪之罪。

items.en: The derived family avaricious and avariciously grew around the noun.
items.cn: 名词周围派生出 avaricious、avariciously 等词族。

note.en: Group one gathers the word's own family and a spelling trap; group two gathers the vocabulary of greed.
note.cn: 第一组收本词词族与一个拼写陷阱；第二组收贪婪义场的词。

entries.definition: the adjective form, greedy for wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式：贪财的、贪婪的。

entries.definition: a female pilot; begins alike but comes from avis, bird.
entries.definitionCN: 女飞行员；开头相近，词源出自 avis「鸟」，与贪婪无关。

entries.definition: both from the same eager root, but avidity is eagerness itself.
entries.definitionCN: 二者同出「渴望」词根，但 avidity 指热切本身，无贬财之意。

entries.definition: the everyday word for insatiable desire, food or wealth included.
entries.definitionCN: 贪婪的常用词，食财皆可指。

entries.definition: greed for money, from Latin cupidus, eager; the formal twin.
entries.definitionCN: 贪财，出自拉丁语 cupidus；avarice 的正式同义词。

entries.definition: the hoarding side of greed, unwillingness to spend.
entries.definitionCN: 吝啬；贪婪中「不肯花」的一面。

entries.definition: aggressive greed that seizes by force or plunder.
entries.definitionCN: 掠夺性的贪婪，以攫取、劫夺为特征。

entries.definition: the drive to acquire and own, neutral to slightly critical.

normalIntro.en: Hold the family together: avere, avarus, avarice, avaricious all share one eager root.
normalIntro.cn: 把词族握在一起：avere、avarus、avarice、avaricious 共享同一个「渴望」词根。

normal.en: Latin avere means to crave: greed is craving locked on money.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 avere 意为渴望：贪婪即锁在钱上的渴望。

normal.en: a-VA-ricious carries the stress of VA-riable greed: always wanting more.
normal.cn: 重音联想：avaricious 的贪像 variable 一样变着花样要更多。

normal.en: Seven-deadly-sins lists pair avarice with charity.
normal.cn: 七宗罪清单中 avarice 与 charity（仁爱）相对。

normal.en: driven by avarice is the set phrase for corrupt motives.
normal.cn: driven by avarice 是描写腐败动机的固定短语。

normal.en: Note the spelling trap: no d in avarice, unlike Avaritia's cousin avidity.
normal.cn: 拼写陷阱：avarice 中没有 d，别与 avidity 混写。

abstract.en: Feel knuckles whiten around a locked purse.
abstract.cn: 感受紧攥钱袋而发白的指节。

abstract.en: Avarice is an appetite that never sits at the table.
abstract.cn: 贪婪是一种从不落座餐桌的胃口。

abstract.en: Picture gold growing heavy until it crushes its keeper.
abstract.cn: 想象金子越来越沉，直到压垮守金之人。

examples.en: Historians blame avarice as much as ambition for the war.
examples.cn: 历史学家认为这场战争源于野心，同样源于贪欲。

examples.en: His avaricious dealings cost the firm its best clients.
examples.cn: 他贪利的交易让公司失去了最好的客户。

examples.en: The old woman's avarice was a shield against a childhood of want.
examples.cn: 老太太的吝啬是抵御童年匮乏的盾牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱挖银丝」——老头爱挖银子攒成丝，一根也不肯花

root: 出自拉丁语 avaritia「贪婪」，基础为 avarus「贪婪的」，源自 avere「热切渴望」；词根一般追溯至印欧语表「希求」的词干。经古法语 avarice 于 13 世纪进入中古英语，长期保留「七宗罪」的道德色彩。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from personal greed for money outward: greed for land, the named vice, hoarding, corrupt motives, the satiric figure, institutional greed, and greed that ruins itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由私人的贪财向外延展：贪图土地、命名之罪、囤积、腐败动机、讽刺形象、集体贪欲，以及自毁的贪婪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand clenched around a purse it will never open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只攥紧钱袋、永不打开的手。

branches.en: THE APPETITE SIDE: craving fixed on money and property.
branches.cn: 欲望一面：锁定钱财与资产的渴望。

branches.en: THE MORAL SIDE: greed as a named, preached-against vice.
branches.cn: 道德一面：作为被命名、被布道声讨的罪。

branches.en: THE HOARDING SIDE: wealth kept, never used.
branches.cn: 囤积一面：只守不用的财富。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC SIDE: motives, caricatures, and corporate vice.
branches.cn: 公共一面：动机、讽刺形象与企业之贪。

branches.en: THE FATAL SIDE: greed that strangles its own holder.
branches.cn: 致命一面：勒住自己的贪欲。

intro.en: Avarice shows the Latin noun ending -itia behind the adjective stem avar-, greedy.
intro.cn: avarice 的结构是形容词干 avar-（贪婪的）加拉丁名词词尾 -itia。

latinIntro.en: Latin built a small family on avere, to crave: avarus, avaritia, and their French and English heirs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 avere「渴望」构建了一个小词族：avarus、avaritia 及其法语、英语后裔。
